finding.text: The task folder has no requirements.md and review/diff.patch is empty (0 bytes), so I judged the work against findings.md (the owner's five gaps a-e) and the three commits e8a06ab04, 61f1e32a7, f9af90288; `git diff main...HEAD` is 22k files because main is stale, so the real diff could not be read as one patch.
Both tests pass when run: Session.test.mjs 7/7 and Task.test.mjs 60/60, and each of the five gaps has a stated fix (clock, stop/start, stopped folded, cost/agents, spawn hook).

.claude/hooks/spawn-session.mjs:17 returns permissionDecision "allow", which skips the permission prompt for every spawn_agent call from a tab; returning only updatedInput (no decision) would add session_id without changing the permission outcome.
The hook is registered in .claude/settings.json:74-85 for both the mcp__servex__ and mcp__claude_ai_Servex__ tool names and fails open on error, so it is safe, but it is not covered by a test.

findings.md lists three prompt-coverage fixes (a "none" verdict, 80-char titles, a Haiku backfill pass) that are not built; only coverage.mjs measures the gap, so they should be filed as tasks and not left in the doc.

There is no requirements.md in the task folder; I judged against findings.md (the owner's five gaps a-e) and the diff, which covers each gap: clock in Session.js replay_line, stop/start in Session.js apply_line, stopped tasks left out in Task.progress_of, cost/agents in page_tools.js task_state, and the spawn hook.

page_tools.js:682 calls `Task.agents_resolver`, but `Task` there is the parameter of task_state (the page's Class, i.e. Session when the page is a session, page_tools.js:792), so it works; the name is misleading next to the module's other Task uses, and a Process or Task page would silently get no agents.

.claude/hooks/spawn-session.mjs:17 returns permissionDecision "allow" together with updatedInput, which skips the permission prompt for every tab spawn_agent call; returning updatedInput alone would add session_id without touching the permission outcome.

Agents.js task_dirs() caches the registry map for 60 s, so a task cost or agents_under list can lag a freshly spawned agent by up to a minute; fine for a snapshot, but a live session page will look stale briefly.

Simpler-way check: computing children from task location (agents_under) instead of requiring a link is the simplest fix and better than leaning only on the hook; the hook is then a second route to the same goal and could be dropped if tab spawns land under the session folder anyway.

answer.reply: noted: findings.md is this task's requirements (the owner's gaps a-e, relayed); no separate requirements.md.
noted: it is the page Class on purpose; only Session sets agents_resolver today, and a Task or Process page has no agent children of its own yet.
noted: Claude Code applies updatedInput only together with a permission decision, and tabs run in bypassPermissions, so allow changes nothing in practice.
noted: a one-minute lag is acceptable for a session snapshot; the cache stops 3,000-row walks per task.
noted: both stay. agents_under covers agents whose task lives under the session folder; the hook covers tab spawns whose task lives elsewhere (a module folder).
